title: Saying sorry and fixing things
examples: What should I say when I accidentally knock over my friend's tower?
If I hurt someone's feelings, how do I make it better?
Can you give me an example of fixing a broken toy?

explain.say: When we make a mistake, we can say sorry. Saying sorry helps our friends know we feel bad.
Fixing things means trying to make things right again. It is about actions, not just words.
Empathy means trying to feel what your friend feels. You put yourself in their shoes.
For example, if you take a toy and break it, you can say sorry and help glue it back together.

draw.text: Say sorry and help fix it.

explain.say: When you accidentally knock over your friend's tower of blocks, you can say sorry. You can then help pick up all the pieces and rebuild it together. This shows you care about their feelings and the toy.

faq.q: What if I don't know how to fix it?
faq.a: It is okay if you do not know how to fix it right away. You can ask a grown-up for help to find a solution together.
asks: What do I do if I break something?
Who can help me fix it?

faq.a: No, saying sorry is just the start. You must also show you are trying to fix the problem or the feeling.
asks: Do I have to do something after I say sorry?

faq.a: You show empathy by noticing how someone looks or sounds. You might ask them, 'Are you okay?'
asks: How do I know if someone is sad?

faq.q: Does fixing things always mean physical things?
faq.a: No, sometimes fixing things means fixing feelings, like giving a hug or listening quietly to a friend.

faq.q: What if my friend gets mad at me?
faq.a: If your friend gets mad, you should stay calm. You can say, 'I see you are upset,' and then listen to them.
asks: What to do when a friend is angry?

facts: Saying sorry is an important part of being a good friend.
Repairing something can mean fixing a toy or fixing a friendship.
Empathy means understanding how someone else feels.
After saying sorry, it is helpful to ask what you can do to help.

quiz.say: You accidentally step on your friend's drawing. What is the first thing you should do?

options.show: Say it was not my fault.
options.say: Say it was not my fault.

quiz.why: Saying sorry shows you know you made a mistake right away.

wrong.1: This makes your friend feel scared and alone.
wrong.2: This makes your friend feel like you do not care about their feelings.
wrong.3: Ignoring it makes your friend feel like their art does not matter.

quiz.say: Your friend is crying because their ball rolled into a puddle. What shows empathy?

options.show: Laugh and say it is silly.
options.say: Laugh and say it is silly.

options.show: Walk away and play with your own toys.
options.say: Walk away and play with your own toys.

quiz.why: Saying what you see helps your friend feel understood.

wrong.0: This tells your friend to stop feeling sad, which is not helpful.
wrong.1: Laughing at someone who is upset makes them feel worse.
wrong.2: Walking away shows you do not care about their sadness.

quiz.say: If you break a crayon box, and your friend says, 'I am really upset,' what is the best way to repair the situation?

options.show: Just give them a new box.
options.say: Just give them a new box.

options.show: Blame the puppy for the mess.
options.say: Blame the puppy for the mess.

options.show: Say sorry and ask, 'How can I help fix it?'
options.say: Say sorry and ask, 'How can I help fix it?'

quiz.why: This combines saying sorry with a plan to fix the problem together.

wrong.0: This only fixes the object, not the feeling of disappointment.
wrong.1: This only explains the event but does not show you care about their feelings.
wrong.2: Blaming someone else does not help you take responsibility for your actions.
